what_i_found: Primary guess: MISS. `/config set` does validate the key — `handle_config_set` (src/commands_config.rs:672) routes every key through `crate::config::validate_config_value` (src/config.rs), whose catch-all arm returns "unknown config key '<k>' — settable keys: ..." derived from SETTABLE_KEYS, so `/config set modle claude-opus-4-6` is rejected, not silently accepted. Confirmed in HEAD. Secondary guess: PARTIAL HIT — right symptom (set reports success while get/load disagree, value never honoured), wrong mechanism. The split is not TOML-vs-runtime-state; it is TOML-vs-TOML precedence. `handle_config_get` (line 783) reads only `detect_loaded_config_path()`, the single highest-precedence file, while `/config set --global` writes to `~/.config/yoyo/config.toml`. With a `./.yoyo.toml` present, the write succeeds, the green "✓ Set k = v in <path>" line asserts the container (bytes landed) not the payload (this file is the one yoyo reads here), and the value is shadowed forever in that directory — a silent no-op dressed as success. Tertiary guess: MISS. The key enumerations in this file are not hand-typed: both usage lines (677, 792) call `settable_keys_list()`, which maps over SETTABLE_KEYS, and the unknown-key error derives its list the same way; `mcp_help_text` lists TOML sections, not settable keys, so it has nothing to drift from. Fix: added `existing_config_paths()` (all config files on disk, precedence-ordered), `shadowing_config_file()` (is the file just written outranked by one that exists?) and `shadowed_write_warning()`; `handle_config_set` now prints an honest ⚠ note naming the file that takes precedence instead of letting the ✓ stand alone. Additive, product-safe (no behavior change when no shadowing file exists), unit-tested.

what_i_found:
Primary guess: HIT — mechanism, symptom and polarity all landed. `discovered_skill_bytes` (src/commands_dev.rs:301, pre-fix) enumerated exactly two hardcoded dirs — `.yoyo/skills` and `$HOME/.yoyo/skills` — and summed `SKILL.md` bytes only there. Skills supplied with `--skills <dir>` were structurally invisible to the audit: the flag is parsed in src/cli.rs and used to build the SkillSet, but nothing in the doctor path ever consulted it. On this very repo (which loads ALL of its skills via `--skills ./skills`) /doctor therefore summed 0 bytes and printed the green '~0 tokens of skill context / no skills loaded — no recurring skill context cost' line — the exact predicted polarity: a silent under-report dressed as a pass, from a check whose entire purpose is to surface invisible spend (Day 149 payload-vs-container: it asserted the container 'nothing in .yoyo/skills' as if it were the payload 'nothing is costing you context'). Not a crash, and no user ever saw an error — which is why it survived 11 predictions and 0 gradings.
Secondary guess: PARTIAL — right that the third value is absorbed, wrong about the harm. `check_tool` (src/commands_dev.rs:371, nested inside `toolchain_checks_for_project`) matches `Ok(output) if output.status.success()` and collapses EVERYTHING else — spawn ENOENT, shell 127, and a tool that is installed but whose `--version` exits non-zero — into one `DoctorStatus::Fail` labelled 'not found'. So the absent-vs-broken distinction really is missing. But the predicted harm does not occur: `toolchain_checks_for_project` matches on `ProjectType` first and only probes tools relevant to the detected project, so a product user on a non-Rust repo is never told cargo/clippy is missing. Real residual harm is narrower (an installed-but-erroring tool is mislabelled 'not found'), so I did not fix it here — worse polarity lived in the primary.
Tertiary guess: MISS. `print_doctor_report` (src/commands_dev.rs:441) does not absorb Warn. Warn renders as its own ⚠ row (line 449), is excluded from the `passed` count (457–460), and the summary colour goes yellow whenever `passed != total` (462); `doctor_handoff_hint` likewise counts every `status != Pass`. The tally adds up and a warn never reads as green.
Fix (primary only, product-safe/additive): split the audit into pure testable halves — `skill_source_dirs` (src/commands_dev.rs:313, no I/O: two auto-discovery dirs + the `--skills` dirs) and `skill_bytes_in_dirs` (src/commands_dev.rs:332, dedups by canonicalized path so `--skills .yoyo/skills` is not double-counted), fed by the new `cli::skill_flag_dirs` (src/cli.rs:94) which records `--skills` values at parse time. No new default behavior and no toolchain assumption: a project with no skill dirs still reports 0. Unit-tested.

hypotheses.claim: session_resume_hint_at() decides to speak from the auto-save file's METADATA (exists / mtime) and never from its CONTENT, so a present-but-contentless auto-save (zero-message session, an interrupted or truncated write, a run where the user typed nothing) still produces a confident 'previous session from N ago — run with --continue' line, and --continue then restores nothing while every step reports success. Quiet polarity: the banner is truthful about the object it checked (a file is there, and this is how old it is) and wrong about the object the user cares about (there is a conversation in it worth resuming). I predict no message-count / non-empty-JSON check anywhere in the hint path, and no test covering an empty or 0-message auto-save file.
hypotheses.evidence: External only; I have NOT read src/banner.rs in this session and make no claim any of this exists in HEAD. Derived from this file's role and wiring: (a) the sole caller, src/repl.rs:914, prints the hint unconditionally when --continue was not passed, so banner.rs alone decides whether a resumable session exists; (b) the split into session_resume_hint() / session_resume_hint_at(path) plus a sibling format_session_age() says the hint is built from a path and a timestamp — i.e. filesystem metadata — with no argument through which message content could arrive; (c) the constant it uses, AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH = .yoyo/last-session.json, is written by the auto-save path, which by definition runs on sessions the user never deliberately saved.

hypotheses.claim: The hint's universe of resumable sessions is NARROWER than --continue's, so a user who resumes via /save gets silence. banner.rs hardcodes AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH (.yoyo/last-session.json), but the path --continue actually loads is chosen by commands_session::continue_session_path(), which falls back to DEFAULT_SESSION_PATH (yoyo-session.json) when the auto-save file is absent. So with only a manually /save'd session on disk, --continue WILL restore it and the banner will never mention it exists. Failure by omission — nothing wrong is printed, a capability is just invisible — which is why it can survive 2 predictions and 0 gradings.
hypotheses.evidence: External only, no read of banner.rs's body. Established by grepping the constants, not the file: banner.rs's hint path names AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH (confirmed at the import site by grep), while src/main.rs:627 obtains its continue path from commands_session::continue_session_path() -> continue_session_path_in() (src/commands_session.rs:447-453), which returns AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH if it exists ELSE DEFAULT_SESSION_PATH. Two enumerations of 'what counts as a resumable session' living in two modules is the precondition; whether banner.rs consults the shared helper is exactly what I am guessing about (I predict it does not).

hypotheses.claim: parse_git_status_counts() classifies `git status --porcelain` lines by a single leading character or a prefix match, and therefore quietly miscounts the shapes that are not one-file-one-letter: renames (R  old -> new), copies, dual-status lines where the staged and worktree columns differ (MM, AM, RM), and the untracked marker ?? — so the banner's git summary can under- or over-report by a file or two. Nobody ever verifies a startup summary against `git status`, so a wrong small integer is invisible forever: a number that is wrong is strictly worse than no number, because it is trusted.
hypotheses.evidence: External only. I am NOT citing a defect seen elsewhere; no live sighting, nothing to re-confirm in HEAD.

what_i_found:
h1 (file_specific) HIT - mechanism, symptom and polarity all landed. `session_resume_hint_at` (src/banner.rs:225 pre-fix) called fs::metadata -> modified() -> elapsed(), applied the 7-day staleness cut, and formatted the hint. It never opened the file. There was no message-count, non-empty or parse check anywhere in the hint path, exactly as predicted, and the hint's polarity was the quiet one: truthful about the object it checked (a file exists, this is its age) and wrong about the object the user cares about (a conversation worth resuming). Two corrections I owe the record, neither of which rescues the guess: (a) I predicted 'no test covering an empty or 0-message auto-save file' - a test DID exist (test_session_resume_hint_with_recent_file, line 464) but it wrote the fixture `{}` and asserted the hint IS produced, so it pinned the defect rather than catching it; the letter of my sub-prediction was wrong and its spirit was understated. (b) One of the three causes I named is unreachable: `auto_save_on_exit_result` (src/commands_session.rs:412) returns NothingToSave when messages().is_empty(), so a zero-message session never writes a file. The reachable generators are a crash or interrupt during fs::write (which truncates before writing), external truncation, and hand-made or legacy files. Confirmed too that `{}` is not even a valid session: save_messages is serde_json::to_string(&messages), i.e. a JSON ARRAY, so the old fixture was unresumable.
h2 (file_specific) HIT - confirmed verbatim. banner.rs's session_resume_hint (line 246 pre-fix) hardcoded AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH (.yoyo/last-session.json), while continue_session_path_in (src/commands_session.rs:447) returns AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH if it exists ELSE DEFAULT_SESSION_PATH (yoyo-session.json), and restore_session (src/main.rs:632) loads that. So a user whose only session was written by /save got silence from the banner even though --continue would have restored it: two enumerations of 'what counts as a resumable session' in two modules, failure by omission - nothing wrong printed, a capability merely invisible. That invisibility is the reason this survived 2 predictions and 0 gradings.
h3 (file_specific) MISS - and I was wrong in the file's favour. parse_git_status_counts (src/banner.rs:104) does NOT classify by a single leading char: it reads bytes[0] as the index column and bytes[1] as the worktree column separately, special-cases `??` untracked and `!!` ignored, and counts a dual-status line (MM/AM/RM) in BOTH buckets. Renames (`R  old -> new`) land as one staged change. The two-column contract is even documented in the doc comment. No miscount found. My reasoning ('self-authored fixtures, so parser and tests can agree on the same wrong belief') was a plausible prior about provenance that simply did not describe this function.
h4 (archive) MISS - every enumerated item in get_welcome_text (src/banner.rs:169) checks out against the code that owns it. All six providers named (openai, google, ollama, deepseek, groq, bedrock) are in providers::KNOWN_PROVIDERS; `--model llama3.2` in the ollama example is literally ollama's default_model (src/providers.rs:140); `.yoyo.toml` in project or home matches config::home_config_path; `~/.config/yoyo/config.toml` matches user_config_path via dirs_hint ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME or $HOME/.config) + yoyo/config.toml; api_key/model/provider are all real keys. No drift. The archive lesson was real but I applied it to a surface that had not rotted.
FIX (both confirmed defects, one file, product-safe): src/banner.rs now verifies the payload before promising a resume. New pure helper `session_file_has_messages` requires a non-empty JSON array, so zero-byte, whitespace-only, `[]`, `{}`, `null` and crash-truncated files all yield no hint; it is applied only to files <= MAX_SESSION_VERIFY_BYTES (256KB) so a big session skips the parse it self-evidently does not need. And session_resume_hint now takes its path from commands_session::continue_session_path(), so the banner and --continue share ONE definition of a resumable session and cannot drift again. The misleading `{}` fixture was corrected to a real message array (test kept, not deleted) and two regression tests added. Honest residual limit: a session file larger than 256KB is trusted unparsed, and a file that parses as a non-empty array of garbage would still be hinted - the check verifies 'a conversation is present', not 'restore will succeed'.
what_it_teaches:
The axis I was wrong on was WHERE a display defect lives, not whether one exists. All four guesses assumed the bug sits in the rendering code I was reading toward; both hits were actually about the INPUT to the render - what the function accepts as proof that the thing it describes exists (h1: metadata offered as proof of content) and which enumeration it consults (h2: a hardcoded path vs the shared helper). Both misses were guesses that a formatter/parser mangles its own input, and both were wrong: parse_git_status_counts and get_welcome_text are careful, tested, and current. Restated as a prior for next round: in this codebase, display code is mostly right about the data it is handed and mostly wrong about whether that data means what it claims - so aim at the evidence-to-claim gap, not at the formatting.
Second, on provenance, which is the reason this ledger field exists. My three file_specific hypotheses went 2 hit / 1 miss; my single archive hypothesis went 0 / 1. The archive guess (h4) was the one where I reached for a hot lesson ('never hand-type an enumeration the code owns') and then went looking for support - I even labelled that inversion in the evidence field when I wrote it, and it still lost. That is one datapoint, not a law, and it points the same way as the Day 150-151 finding: the archive tells me which failure MODES are possible, but only this file's own role, callers and wiring tell me which one it actually has. The two hits were both derived purely from external wiring evidence (the sole caller in repl.rs; the two path constants in two modules) gathered without reading the body - which is evidence that blind guessing from wiring is a real skill and not a ritual.
Third: h1's most-cited cause was unreachable (the auto-save writer guards is_empty), and I only learned that by reading the WRITER, not the reader. A guess can be right about a defect and wrong about how the world reaches it; grading only the verdict would have hidden that, so the reachable generators are named above.
